db_evidence.notes: Both clue windows are retrievable via plain SQL on the episodes table at 30sec granularity. Shrine 2 (Mount Huaguo/Qingzhang, 77065-77080) is described almost verbatim: row 77070-77100 literally states 'the player at level 27 with 675 health, 92 vigor' (captioner mislabeled which field is level vs vigor, but the numbers 675 and 92 are both present and correct), so any rollout landing a query/clip_qa within roughly 77040-77130 recovers the right answer -- 4 of 5 rollouts did (only rollout 0 missed it, landing at 78510-78540). Shrine 1 (Flaming Mountains/Huo Liao, 63374-63389) is harder: the 30sec row exactly covering the unlock (63390-63420) mentions 'a dark shrine menu with two flaming sword-pillars' but does NOT contain the literal place-name keywords 火焰山/火燎一关 (those appear only ~30-60s later, in an unrelated fast-travel menu at 63420-63450). A keyword LIKE search on the coarse 3min table (episodes:3min:000352, 63360-63540) does match because its merged summary text includes 火焰山, which is how rollout 1 (the only fully correct one) found it. Narrower 30sec-level or off-by-30s time-window queries (rollouts 2/3/4) missed or skipped the exact shrine-menu row, and rollout 4 even retrieved the correct row but failed to act on it.

root_causes: The shrine-1 unlock moment's 30-second episode caption does not contain the location name keyword (火焰山/火燎一关), only 'shrine menu'/'flaming sword-pillars' language; only a coarser 3-minute merged row or a sufficiently wide multi-keyword LIKE query surfaces it, so most rollouts' keyword/time-window searches for shrine 1 missed it entirely or by tens of seconds

Off-by-30-second time-window run_sql queries (rollout 3: BETWEEN 63420-63780, excluding the 63390-63420 row) silently drop the one row containing the decisive text, with no signal to the agent that it clipped the boundary

Semantic_search embeddings for shrine 1 repeatedly surfaced unrelated later shrine-interaction clips (e.g. ~70860-71160, ~75000-75500, ~65700-66120) that visually resemble a 'shrine unlock' scene, pulling several rollouts away from the true 63374-63389 window before any keyword search corrected them

Rollout 4 retrieved the correct row (63390-63420, containing the literal shrine-menu text) in its own SQL output but did not select/act on it, instead continuing to a different, wrong candidate window -- a retrieved-but-not-used evidence failure
Shrine 2 (Mount Huaguo) was comparatively easy: the exact clue window's caption states the numeric stats plainly, so 4/5 rollouts recovered 675/92 correctly regardless of shrine-1 outcome
what_worked: Rollout 1's broad 4-keyword LIKE query across all candidate place names (not narrowed to only one location or a tight time window) matched a coarse 3-minute episode row whose merged summary happened to include the target place name, correctly anchoring shrine 1
For shrine 2, querying/clip_qa'ing directly inside or very near the clue window (77040-77220) reliably recovered the correct 675/92 in 4 of 5 rollouts since the caption states the numbers explicitly
transferable_lessons: For 'value at the moment of unlocking X' questions, do not rely solely on time-window run_sql queries with hand-picked boundaries -- boundaries offset by even 30 seconds can exclude the single row containing the decisive text; prefer keyword LIKE search across multiple location-name variants and multiple granularities (30sec and 3min) rather than committing early to a time window inferred from a different, coarser hit

When a run_sql result already contains a row whose text closely matches the question ('dark shrine menu', 'flaming sword-pillars'), the agent should verify/act on it with clip_qa before pivoting to a different candidate window found via unrelated semantic search

Location-name keywords used in a question may not appear in the caption of the exact unlock-moment clip; the on-screen menu/action text ('shrine menu', 'flaming sword-pillars', 'incense/上香') is often the more reliable text anchor than the place name itself, which may only appear in an adjacent clip (e.g. a subsequent fast-travel menu)

When multiple candidate windows exist for the same clue, prefer the one whose SQL caption text most literally describes the shrine/UI interaction described in the question, not the one visually closest to an unrelated but similar-looking shrine scene surfaced by semantic search
open_questions: Whether the episode captioning pipeline could be improved to include location-name keywords in the exact unlock-moment 30-second caption, which would make this class of question far easier to retrieve deterministically

Why rollout 4 retrieved the exact correct row via SQL but still chose to clip_qa a different, wrong window instead -- likely a reasoning/selection lapse not observable in the (encrypted) reasoning trace
